reproduction:
python3 - <<'EOF'
from spacy.vocab import Vocab

vocab = Vocab()
_ = vocab["dog"]
assert "dog" in vocab
try:
    with vocab.memory_zone():
        _ = vocab["horse"]
        raise ValueError("simulated error")
except ValueError:
    pass

assert not vocab.in_memory_zone, "Vocab stuck in memory-zone state after an exception"
assert "dog" in vocab
assert "horse" not in vocab, "transient word from failed memory zone leaked"
lex = vocab["cat"]
assert lex.text == "cat"
print("REPRO-OK: memory zone cleaned up after exception")
EOF
(pytest alternative: python -m pytest spacy/tests/vocab_vectors/test_memory_zone.py::test_memory_zone_exception_cleanup -q)
observed_failure_at_parent: AssertionError: Vocab stuck in memory-zone state after an exception (assert not vocab.in_memory_zone fails: in_memory_zone is True after the exception). pytest: test_memory_zone_exception_cleanup FAILED, 1 failed / 3 passed in the file. The contextlib cleanup after `yield mem` in Vocab.memory_zone / StringStore.memory_zone never runs when an exception propagates, so the vocab stays in memory-zone state and transient strings are leaked.
verified: Both directions observed in a bench-base:python-3.12 container (spaCy 3.8.11, numpy 2.5.3, thinc 8.3.11, python 3.12.13): at parent_commit (extensions rebuilt) the standalone repro and the upstream regression test fail as described; at fix_commit (extensions rebuilt) both pass. Buggy code confirmed present at parent by inspection (`yield mem` not wrapped in try/finally in strings.pyx/vocab.pyx). CRITICAL trap hit during verification: the compiled Cython extensions (.so) survive `git reset --hard`, so after switching parent<->fix you MUST `rm -f spacy/*.so` and rebuild, otherwise the stale fix-era binaries mask the bug (my first parent run falsely showed the test passing because the .so still contained the fix).
install_recipe:

cd <checkout> && git config --global --add safe.directory <checkout>
git reset --hard <sha> && git clean -fd
python3 -m pip install -r requirements.txt    # full test deps: pytest, pytest-timeout, mock, hypothesis, mypy, ...

python3 -c 'import spacy; print(spacy.__version__)'   # expect 3.8.11
issue_paraphrase: spaCy 3.8+ added a context-manager API for bounding memory usage when processing large volumes of text: entering a memory zone makes all new vocabulary strings and lexemes transient, and leaving the zone frees them. But if an exception is raised inside the with-block, the cleanup that should restore normal vocabulary memory never runs. Afterwards the vocabulary permanently reports that it is still inside a memory zone, words created during the failed block are either leaked or freed at the wrong time, and further lookups and additions can crash or corrupt the vocabulary. Anyone catching an exception around a memory zone (for example a server processing documents under a memory budget) is left with a corrupted, unusable vocabulary.
fix_summary: Wrapped the `yield mem` in both `Vocab.memory_zone` and `StringStore.memory_zone` in try/finally so the transient-string cleanup and the memory-pool reset always run even when an exception propagates through the context manager. New regression test test_memory_zone_exception_cleanup asserts the vocab is not stuck in zone state and transient words are removed after an exception.
notes: Verified 2026-09-11 on bench-base:python-3.12 (Debian trixie, py3.12.13). Suite runs in <1s at 64 cores; expect a few seconds at 1 CPU. No network needed at test time. The fix-era tree is spaCy 3.8.11 (March 2026) and its full transitive dependency set does NOT collide with tb21_source_repositories.json (langcodes was removed from spaCy in May 2025, #13760). Build takes a few minutes on this host, longer at 1 CPU; instruct trials that the container needs build-essential. The three pre-existing tests in the file (no_insertion/insertion/redundant_insertion) also pass at the parent; only test_memory_zone_exception_cleanup is the regression signal. If the trial only greps for try/finally it will find nothing at parent: the parent simply has no cleanup wrapper. Memory-zone API is niche but the repro is self-contained and the failure message is explicit.

issue_paraphrase: Rendering annotations to HTML for Jupyter notebooks via the dependency/entity visualiser (displacy) crashes with an ImportError on recent IPython versions: calling the render function with Jupyter output enabled imports a display helper from a deprecated IPython module path that newer IPython releases removed. The user-visible symptom is a hard crash (ImportError: cannot import name 'display' from 'IPython.core.display') exactly when trying to visualise a document in a notebook, so the rendering workflow is entirely broken on up-to-date IPython installs.
fix_summary: Split the IPython import: keep `from IPython.core.display import HTML` and import `display` from the current `IPython.display` module, which exists across IPython versions. (IPython.core.display.display was deprecated in 8.x and removed in 9.) No regression test was added upstream.
notes: Verified 2026-09-11 on bench-base:python-3.12 with ipython 9.17.1. Runtime ~1s; no network needed at test time once ipython is installed. The fix-era tree (spaCy 3.8.7, Oct 2025) is after the langcodes removal (#13760, May 2025), so nothing in its transitive dependency set collides with tb21_source_repositories.json (checked each requirement name). jupyter=True must be passed explicitly: outside a real notebook `is_in_jupyter()` is False. With ipython<9 the parent does not fail (old path still exists), so the task image must install ipython>=9 — recent pip images will already have it; pin it in the recipe to be safe. The parent/fix commits differ in a single pure-Python file, so compiled extensions stay valid across the reset (no rebuild needed between states for this one).
